newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah weakens on dollar short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah weakens on dollar short-covering.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah weakened against the U.S. currency on short-covering in dollars in moderate early trading on Wednesday , dealers said.
One U.S. bank dealer said the rupiah strengthened at the opening to 2,453 from 2,455 and the New York closing of 2,458/59, but slid back to 2,457/78 at 0225 GMT.
"I think it's a combination of dollar short-covering ahead of Thursday's public holiday and ample liquidity," the dealer said, adding volume was relatively high.
All markets will be closed on Thursday for the birthday of Prophet Muhammad and reopen on Friday.
Dealers said trading was not as dramatic as Monday, but the market remained edgy on on-going volatility in the region.
They said operators were not fully comfortable and remained cautious of a possible spillover if sentiment changed.
However, one Japanese bank dealer said spreads were narrowing, suggesting improved confidence in the market.

"There is good demand from both local and foreign side but supply is also sufficient. People don't want to be caught too long or too short if other markets turn naughty on Thursday," another dealer said.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,455.25/56.50 and 2,454.75/56.00, respectively.
Liquidity was ample for now, with overnight rates traded at around 8.0/9.0 percent in the morning. Overnight swap was at 0.3/0.4 and tom/next at 0.6/0.7 points.
The U.S. bank dealer said swap rates were edging up after easing at the opening, suggesting some volatility remained.
But he said local operators were taking profits on foreign selling, limiting sharp declines in swap premiums.
Offshore operators had stocked up rupiah with swaps previously to prepare for a possible squeeze by the central bank to fend off speculation.
But the bank had pursued an unchanged monetary policy, generating arbitrage opportunity for local players with cheap rupiah funds to fill foreign appetite for swaps.
"Now local players are cashing out and limited a quick adjustment in swap rates," one Japanese bank dealer said.
He said offshore operators had to lift swap prices higher before they could unload their positions, otherwise the losses were too large.
One-month swap was at 18.0/20.0, two at 37.0/40.0, three at 55.0/59.0 and six at 105/1.09 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,376/2,680 but lowered the conversion band to 2,425/2,473 on Tuesday -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364.
